rules: A clean outcome on all three deciding events (budget part 1 passes, Moody's affirms, gilts calm after the Budget) is a same-day catalyst: taking T2 together with T1 is then defensible. Not a trigger by itself.

An escalation outcome on any one deciding event ends re-entry on the fizzle path: no tranche is bought, every filled tranche is reviewed against the bear-path levels — a user step off-run, not a skill call.

brief.fund: EXSH (`EXSH.DE`) — a 30-stock dividend basket, never a euro-bank fund: ~62% financials (life insurers + UK/NL banks), ~29% UK (gilts/GBP matter, not only Bunds/ECB), ~21% NL, ~24% France of which banks ≈ 6% (French sovereign risk is an indirect channel). Composition as of 2026-08-31; re-ask the user when stale.
brief.holdsPolicy: `holds: ["T2","T3"]` on the deciding events (the French budget votes, Moody's, the UK Budget); a fizzle outcome frees them on the next run, with no pad — the relief is mostly priced on day 0–1.
brief.gates: The UK Budget is also a gate inside the fast set's T2/T3 tally — the same event, not a second signal.
brief.eventScope: French or UK sovereign debt, or the UK bank tax

signs.label: CHANGED
signs.finding: Fitch moved France's outlook to negative from stable in an unscheduled review on 10-30, affirming A+ and citing a credit profile that deteriorated since its August review, a 2027 deficit it sees staying wide and a third-quarter GDP contraction; it credits the banks' capital buffers with limiting the state's contingent liabilities and sets its next review by end-February 2027 (Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance 10-30). No cut, no French-bank rating action. Moody's kept Aa3 negative on 10-23 (its rating assumes a deficit-cutting 2027 budget is adopted). S&P sits A+ stable and reviews Italy 11-13 and France 11-27 (orafinanza, AFT). Italy: Moody's Baa2 stable 09-25, no November review
signs.why: a downgrade can force sellers out (index and collateral rules) and drag the country's banks down with it (Moody's cut 7 French banks in Dec 2024)
signs.measurable: date yes, outcome no; BLOCKING = a sovereign or bank downgrade · draft: escalation-leaning = an agency cuts France, Italy or the UK, or puts a bank of theirs on review for downgrade ; open = a review is dated inside the window with no outcome yet ; fizzle-leaning = the dated review affirms the rating or only moves the outlook ; quiet = no review dated inside the window

signs.label: UNCHANGED 10-28
signs.finding: The solemn vote on the PLF 2027 revenue part stays dated 11-03 (afternoon) after the article-by-article examination running 10-27 to 11-02; the ensemble vote is 11-17 and the 70-day constitutional clock runs out 12-09 (Assemblée agenda, franceinfo). No 49.3 and no censure motion: the dossier's newest entries are committee opinions of 10-22 and 10-28, no public-session entry since 10-13 (Assemblée dossier, read 11-02). Earlier: the PS motion de rejet préalable was rejected 236–149 on 10-13 with the RN voting against it so the debate runs; commission rejected the revenue part 31–3 on 10-09. Standing positions: Glucksmann 'pas de censure a priori' but censure if the text does not move; Lescure does not rule out ordinances; LFI would censure on 49.3; RN 'jamais de censure automatique', pension de-indexation a red line. Adoption before year-end uncertain (abcbourse 10-21)
signs.why: a fallen government with no budget leaves the deficit unaddressed and the risk carries into the April 2027 election; in Dec 2024 and Sep 2025 spreads repriced, but banks recovered within months
signs.measurable: dates yes; BLOCKING = none (context row) · draft: escalation-leaning = a censure motion is filed or announced, the government invokes 49.3 on the revenue part, or a loi spéciale / ordinances are announced ; open = the debate runs with censure threatened but neither filed nor withdrawn ; fizzle-leaning = the PS or RN says it will not censure, a deal is reported, or part 1 passes a solemn vote ; quiet = no budget-vote news inside the window

signs.label: CHANGED
signs.finding: The 10-29 decision text names the TPI as 'available to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics' and the Council 'stands ready to adjust all of its instruments'; asked about French spreads, Lagarde said instruments are available for unwarranted and disorderly moves under published criteria, that there is 'no behind-the-scene arrangement', that redemptions keep running off without purchases, and that 'November is a pretty heavy month when it comes to France' (ECB 10-29). Tools named, conditions not declared met, no buying. Earlier: Lagarde mid-October 'the first solution lies at home in France'; BdF's Moulin 10-16 saw no fragmentation
signs.why: without a backstop, spreads can keep widening (2011 until LTRO / "whatever it takes")

signs.label: UNCHANGED 10-30
signs.finding: Fitch's 10-30 outlook move to negative on France explicitly credits the banking sector's capital buffers with limiting contingent liabilities for the state, and took no bank action (Yahoo Finance 10-30); Moody's left the French banks untouched on 10-23. Lagarde was asked on 10-29 why French banks' sovereign holdings fell less than Italian or German peers and gave no supervisory signal (ECB 10-29). French sovereign protection is at its dearest since 2013 (finews 10-22); French banks still trade as proxies for the sovereign, their 5y CDS above European peers (AlphaValue via S&P Global MI 10-13; Bloomberg via France Épargne 10-05); ACPR calls their domestic sovereign holdings small relative to assets. No bank-specific CDS print or supervisory action in the window (ECB banking supervision feed through 10-30)
signs.why: banks loaded with home-country bonds take losses, funding gets dearer, and the state has to back the banks (Italy 2018, 2011)

situation.lean: The leg leans fizzle: the UK Budget and the ECB both passed without a shock, leaving the French revenue-part ballot on 11-03 as the last hold on the deeper tranches. Nothing is bought until it passes.
situation.slow: The grind is the French sovereign: Fitch has joined Moody's on a negative outlook, French sovereign protection stays the dearest in over a decade, and the ECB calls November a heavy month for France while declining to buy. Bank earnings and capital hold, so the de-rating is still a spread story, not a credit-loss one.
situation.fast: The gap is the 11-03 ballot: a filed censure motion, a 49.3 on the revenue part or a slide into a loi spéciale would reprice French paper past its peak, with Moody's and Fitch both tying their ratings to a deficit-cutting budget. A December ECB hike into wide spreads is the second gap, now openly signalled.
situation.decides: The French revenue-part ballot on 11-03 moves the fast slot: passage or a no-censure pledge frees the last hold, a censure filing or a 49.3 blocks. S&P on Italy 11-13 and on France 11-27 move the slow slot, and the ECB in December moves the fast slot if it hikes.
situation.flips: A PS or RN no-censure pledge or a passed revenue part moves the lean to fizzle and frees the holds; a filed censure motion, a 49.3, a loi spéciale or an agency cut moves it to escalation-leaning and blocks.
